prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity compact native macOS approval review concept, one complete screen.
Primary request: Visualize the proposed HEAV3NS-CODE design at a compact 720 by 500 point window, with a native approval review sheet open. Keep the entire window, sheet, and bottom composer visible. This belongs to the same app as the supplied wide light workspace concept. Show focused review of a specific operation, with clear controls and enough readable detail.
Input images: image 1 is the generated light workspace design and establishes refined system typography, native light materials, restrained controls and blue selection. Image 2 is the actual app's approval sheet and establishes operation scope and the Close / Deny / Allow Once hierarchy. Use their product truth and native identity, not their exact contents or dark palette. This new compact concept uses light Aqua.
Composition: flat orthographic screenshot of one complete native window, 1440 by 1000 pixels if supported, 1.44:1 ratio. No device, wallpaper, perspective, decorative frame, annotations, or presentation slide. Unified toolbar at top, navigation sidebar hidden at this compact width. Background work area shows a centered segmented control "Agent" and "Inspect", Agent selected, a short conversation, and a composer pinned to the bottom. A native sheet of about 620 by 340 points sits centered in the usable window with comfortable 20-point internal padding and subtle system shadow. All three decision buttons must be fully visible and readable.
Window toolbar: standard traffic lights, compact sidebar-toggle icon, title "LUMI-NEW", smaller subtitle "HEAV3NS-CODE"; status "Waiting for review", a Stop button, and ellipsis Actions control. Avoid tiny crammed text. Background conversation has author "You" with "Check the native layout." and a LUMI response "I need approval to run the next command." Keep the background gently dimmed, with the bottom text composer still visible and a footer showing "Up Next (1)" and "Queue". The sheet has focus.
Sheet: prominent but restrained heading "Review Request" and smaller operation label "run_command". Three compact well-separated sections in a scrollable native text region. Labels in system semibold; values in readable system mono where appropriate. Exact content: "Workspace", "/workspace/LUMI-NEW", "Reason", "Run the native checks for this workspace.", "Arguments", "{", "  \"command\": \"swift test --package-path native\"", "}". Ensure the entire command remains visible without clipping. A plain explanation below the details reads "Allow Once applies only to this operation." A second line reads "Close leaves the request waiting." Bottom button row: "Close" at far left; "Deny" and "Allow Once" at far right. All three are neutral native buttons of equal emphasis. Allow Once is NOT blue, NOT the default Return action, and has NO focus halo. No scary destructive red treatment or shield illustration.
Style: refined light Aqua macOS, white detail area, cool pale system gray sheet and toolbar, crisp near-black primary text and sufficiently dark secondary text. San Francisco-like system typography, 14-point readable body, 13-point controls, 12-point details. Sheet title around 17 points. Standard native rounded corners and precise geometry, restrained depth, real-looking compact window chrome. No giant alert symbol, card collage, chunky outlines, gradients, halos, or glass decoration.
Constraints: This is a proposed compact review layout with illustrative data, not an actual permission request. Keep the familiar existing capability and native app identity. Do not introduce new capabilities, changes approval/apply buttons, multiple modal layers, permanent permission switches, a default approval action, editor tabs, or dashboard metrics. All visible actionable controls must look appropriately sized and contained within the window.
